title: Private VPC: Connectivity Profiles and Upgrade Modes for Air-limited Deployments
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Define and validate a minimal-but-complete requirements set and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC customers that operate in severely constrained network environments (outbound-only, ephemeral egress windows, or fully air-limited sites). This ticket standardizes 'connectivity profiles', prescribes supported upgrade modes (online, staged-mirror, signed-media), clarifies artifact delivery expectations, and lists operational validation steps required for GA. Goal: enable predictable, auditable upgrades and connectivity behaviour for customers with strict egress/air-gap controls without introducing silent failures or security regressions.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private in regulated environments request deterministic upgrade behavior and clear networking contracts. Existing edge cases (e.g., intermittent proxy-only egress, restricted DNS, long maintenance windows) have caused failed upgrades, unclear rollback triggers, and mismatched operator expectations. Product needs a compact PRD that defines connectivity profiles, upgrade orchestration flows, acceptance tests, and operator runbook items so SRE and operators can certify customer installs against a documented compatibility matrix.
requirements: Connectivity profiles: define three canonical profiles (Full-Managed: bi-directional control-plane and telemetry; Outbound-Limited: TLS outbound to allowlist endpoints only; Isolated-Air-Limited: no outbound; operator provides signed artifacts).
Network contract: list of resolvable FQDNs and CIDRs for each profile plus explicit DNS/MTU/HTTP proxy expectations and minimal port list (TCP 443, optional 53/UDP via configured resolver).

Upgrade modes: support and document three modes: online-pull (standard), staged-mirror (customer mirrors validated set of images/artifacts to internal registry), signed-media (physical or secure transfer of signed TARs with manifest).

Artifact provenance: every offline/staged artifact bundle must be signed (image manifest + checksum + catalog.json) using Redwood key-rotation policy; operator will validate signatures before applying.

Operator agent capabilities: private operator must support dry-run validation, dependency-check (K8s CRDs, node image compatibility), and preflight artifact checksum verification. Failure modes must be surfaced with explicit remediation steps.

Telemetry and observability: for Outbound-Limited profile, provide a minimal consented telemetry bundle (heartbeat + upgrade status + non-sensitive error codes) that can be forwarded through a customer proxy. For Isolated-Air-Limited, provide an artifact-only attestation report that the operator can retrieve post-upgrade.

Maintenance windows and rollback policy: upgrades must be staged with configurable max downtime, automatic rollback on >X% critical agent failure, and a manual immediate rollback trigger with documented steps.
KMS constraints: define KMS rotation expectations during an upgrade (no external KMS calls for Isolated-Air-Limited during window unless allowed).

Upgrade verification tests: post-upgrade smoke checks (control plane API responsiveness, model-serving readiness, KV cache integrity checks, key services started) and a deterministic health-check script customers can run offline.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Connectivity profile matrix published (Full-Managed, Outbound-Limited, Isolated-Air-Limited) with required ports, DNS expectations, proxy headers, and example firewall rules.

A2: Private operator supports three upgrade modes end-to-end: online-pull, staged-mirror (pull from customer mirror), and signed-media apply. Each mode has documented operator steps and automated preflight validation.
A3: Signed artifact format spec and verification tool delivered; tool verifies manifest signatures, image checksums, and component compatibility offline.
A4: Rollback contract (timeout thresholds, failure signals, and operator rollback runbook) documented and validated in an integration lab against simulated partitioned networks.
A5: Minimal telemetry bundle defined and implemented for Outbound-Limited; privacy-preserving attestation artifact for Isolated-Air-Limited is generated and verifiable after upgrade.
A6: Security review completed and checklist items resolved (image signing keys, operator RBAC scope, offline key handling).
A7: Customer-facing onboarding doc and quick-check script published; at least two customer beta installs complete a signed-media upgrade and report post-upgrade attestation.
A8: E2E test matrix executed in CI with simulated proxy, intermittent DNS failures, and maximum MTU mismatch; test results pass with documented mitigations for known failure modes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Spec): finalize connectivity profiles, signed-artifact spec, and operator preflight requirements (2 sprints).
Phase 2 (Implementation): deliver artifact-verifier CLI, operator preflight checks, and minimal telemetry channel for Outbound-Limited (3 sprints).
Phase 3 (Lab Validation): run upgrade scenarios in isolated testbeds (signed-media, mirror, online) including rollback rehearsals (1 sprint).
Phase 4 (Customer Beta): enable with 3 pilot customers (one per profile) and iterate on runbooks and edge-case fixes (4 weeks).
Phase 5 (GA): publish docs, enable by default in private-operator-2.3 with feature flags and support bundles.
test_plan: Unit tests for artifact verifier and manifest signer validation.
Integration tests: operator preflight against a fake mirror registry and a signed-media bundle applied to a cluster in an isolated subnet.
Chaos tests: simulate DNS outage during upgrade and verify rollback triggers and operator alerts.
Manual acceptance: runbook-driven signed-media upgrade on staging and produce attestation report; verification by security reviewer.
Performance: ensure upgrade orchestration does not extend node drain time by >20% compared to baseline in the lab.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers misconfigure DNS/proxy and block health checks -> Mitigation: provide an automated network-checker with clear remediation steps and preflight failure codes.

Risk: Signed-media handling leads to key compromise if operators mishandle private keys -> Mitigation: document secure key handling, recommend HSM/KMS patterns, and require signature verification tooling that rejects unsigned bundles.

Risk: Telemetry constraints reduce our ability to triage failures -> Mitigation: define a minimal, opt-in diagnostic bundle and a secure on-prem attestation report that contains detailed, non-sensitive failure codes.
Risk: Mirror sync drift causing version mismatches -> Mitigation: include a catalog.json with content hashes and a registry-scan preflight step that rejects incomplete mirrors.
success_metrics: Metric: 95% of beta private installs complete signed-media or mirror upgrades without manual intervention.
Metric: 0 customer upgrade incidents attributable to unclear network expectations in the first 6 months after GA.
Metric: Preflight checker adoption by >=80% of new Private customers within first contact.
Metric: Time to remediate a failed upgrade (operator intervention to healthy state) < 4 hours for 90% of incidents in lab runs.
notes: This PRD intentionally focuses on deterministic upgrade behavior and a compact network contract rather than exhaustive networking hardening. Follow-on tickets should expand to multi-region air-limited replication and physical media courier integrations.
